chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the salat in the month of Ramadan, and he said: Thirteen rakʿahs, including the witr and two rakʿahs before salat al-fajr. If it had been an additional merit, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would have acted upon it more and been more deserving of it.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) being asked about
key_terms.الْوِتْرُ: the witr prayer included within the total
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً: thirteen rakʿahs as the stated number of prayers
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose practice is used as proof
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time under discussion
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer, before which two rakʿahs are mentioned
key_terms.فَضْلًا: extra merit or added virtue beyond what is established

ai.seo_question: How many rakʿahs are prescribed for salat in the month of Ramadan according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat in the month of Ramadan, stating a total of thirteen rakʿahs including al-witr and the two rakʿahs before fajr. It also grounds the ruling in the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, indicating that any truly superior additional practice would have been most fitting for him to perform.
